name: Thakurgaon
tagline: Asia's largest mango tree, a Tonknath rajbari, and the quiet north-west cousin of Panchagarh.

guide.bestTime: October to March for the cool, dry season; May–July to see the Suryapuri mango trees in fruit
guide.gettingThere: By train to Thakurgaon Road station on the far-northern line, or by road from Dhaka (~10–11 hr), Rangpur (~2.5 hr) and Saidpur airport (~75 km). No airport in the district.
guide.difficulty: Easy — flat terrain, cool weather, short upazila hops by CNG and easybike.

mustVisit.name: Suryapuri Mango Tree of Harinmari (Baliadangi)
mustVisit.description: A roughly 200-year-old Suryapuri mango tree at Mandumala village near the Indian border — claimed as the largest mango tree in Asia, its branches spreading across about an acre of ground.
mustVisit.history: The tree stands 80–90 feet tall with a trunk girth around 35 feet and a canopy covering some 2.5 bighas. It still bears a full crop each year of the regional Suryapuri variety, the mango that has made Baliadangi upazila famous. A small team of caretakers tends it season after season.

howToReach.fromDistrictTown: About 35 km west of Thakurgaon town in Mandumala village, Harinmari block, Baliadangi Upazila
howToReach.transport: Bus or CNG to Baliadangi, then easybike to Harinmari

mustVisit.bestTime: May to July for fruiting; cool months for a quiet visit
tips: It sits very close to the India border — keep your NID handy
Combine with the Harinmari Shiv Mandir just nearby

mustVisit.name: Jamalpur Zamindar Bari Jame Mosque
mustVisit.description: An ornate three-domed brick mosque with twenty-eight minarets on its roof, built by the Jamalpur zamindars in 1867 and listed under the Department of Archaeology of Bangladesh.
mustVisit.history: Zamindar Jamal Uddin, a descendant of Roshan Ali of the Tajpur Parganas in West Bengal, laid the foundation of his estate house in 1862 and began the mosque in 1867. The mosque was completed before the family home, and remains in active use; it holds about 300–600 worshippers.

practical.hours: Open during five daily prayers; visitors welcome outside prayer times

howToReach.fromDistrictTown: In Jamalpur union, ~10 km from Thakurgaon town

mustVisit.bestTime: Outside Friday noon prayers; morning light
tips: Cover head if female; remove shoes before stepping onto the platform
The 28 roof minarets are best seen from the courtyard

mustVisit.name: Raja Tonknath Rajbari (Ranisankail)
mustVisit.description: The brick palace of Raja Tonknath at Ranisankail, set among old tanks and shrines — including a Ramchandra temple just outside the main gate.
mustVisit.history: Built by the 19th-century zamindar Tonknath of the Mahishpota estate, the rajbari combines a red-brick European façade with traditional Bengali courtyards and family temples. Parts of the building are ruined but the scale and ornament still carry the old zamindari.

howToReach.fromDistrictTown: About 30 km south-west of Thakurgaon town in Ranisankail Upazila
howToReach.transport: Bus or CNG to Ranisankail, then easybike to the rajbari

tips: Walk around the back to see the Ramchandra temple
Be careful with the failing upper masonry — exterior viewing only

mustVisit.name: Harinmari Shiv Mandir (Baliadangi)
mustVisit.description: A small, roughly 400-year-old Shiva temple at Harinmari Haat, square in plan with a charchala roof and terracotta panels of creeper-motif figures on its south wall.

howToReach.fromDistrictTown: At Harinmari Haat, ~35 km from Thakurgaon town in Baliadangi Upazila
howToReach.transport: CNG to Baliadangi, then easybike to Harinmari

mustVisit.bestTime: Shivaratri (Feb–Mar) for the festival; cool months otherwise
tips: Photograph the south-wall terracotta in soft side-light
Pair with the Suryapuri mango tree, which is right next door

mustVisit.name: Balia Mosque
mustVisit.description: A small three-domed brick mosque with eight slender minarets — almost identical to a miniature of the Jamalpur mosque — and a local legend that jinns raised it overnight on a new-moon night.
mustVisit.history: Listed by the Department of Archaeology of Bangladesh as a historical structure. The dome was reportedly the last element added — local folklore holds that the unfinished work was the jinns' incomplete share.

practical.hours: Open during five daily prayers; visitors welcome outside prayer times

howToReach.fromDistrictTown: In Balia, Thakurgaon Sadar, ~12 km from town

mustVisit.bestTime: Outside Friday noon prayers; golden hour
tips: Cover head if female; remove shoes
Pair with the Jamalpur mosque on the same morning

mustVisit.name: Tangon Riverbank, Thakurgaon Town
mustVisit.description: The slow Tangon river runs along the western edge of Thakurgaon town — a quiet evening walk with a wooden footbridge, fishing boats and old gachhi (date-palm-sap) trees in winter.

howToReach.fromDistrictTown: On the western edge of Thakurgaon town
howToReach.transport: Rickshaw or on foot from the town centre

tips: Combine with grilled corn at the embankment stalls
Stalls are quiet on weekday afternoons

specialties.name: Suryapuri Mango
specialties.description: The slim, golden-orange mango of Baliadangi — sweet, fragrant and the variety the district is named for in fruit-lover circles. Most of the country's Suryapuri orchards are here.

specialties.name: Pelka
specialties.description: A regional north-Bengal vegetable curry of greens cooked with kalai-flour balls — slow-simmered, earthy, and traditional to Thakurgaon and the wider Rangpur belt.

specialties.name: Kolai Ruti & Sidol Bhorta
specialties.description: Thick gram-flour rotis paired with pungent fermented-fish sidol bhorta, the standard farmer's breakfast of the region.

specialties.name: Suryapuri Mango Season
specialties.description: Late May into July is the great Suryapuri season — orchard hopping, mango-tasting visits to Mandumala, and the haats around Baliadangi alive with crates of fruit.

bucketlist.title: Stand under Asia's largest mango tree
bucketlist.detail: A 200-year-old Suryapuri at Mandumala spreading across about an acre — 80–90 feet tall, 35-foot girth, still bearing a full crop every summer.

bucketlist.title: Eat a fresh Suryapuri mango in season
bucketlist.detail: The slim golden mango that gave the district its mango fame — at its sweetest a few hours after the morning pluck.

bucketlist.title: Count the 28 minarets of Jamalpur Mosque
bucketlist.detail: Three domes and twenty-eight slim roof minarets — built by the Jamalpur zamindar in 1867, still in daily prayer.

bucketlist.title: Explore Raja Tonknath's rajbari at Ranisankail
bucketlist.detail: A 19th-century red-brick palace with European façades and Bengali courtyards, with a Ramchandra temple just outside the gate.

bucketlist.title: See the terracotta creepers at Harinmari Shiv Mandir
bucketlist.detail: A ~400-year-old charchala-roofed Shiva temple with terracotta panels of creeper-motif figures along its south wall.

bucketlist.title: Visit the jinn-built Balia Mosque
bucketlist.detail: A small three-domed mosque with eight minarets, listed by the Department of Archaeology — local lore says jinns raised it in one night.

bucketlist.title: Walk the Tangon riverbank at dusk
bucketlist.detail: A slow river along the western edge of town, with a wooden footbridge, fishing boats and embankment stalls grilling corn in winter.

bucketlist.title: Try pelka at a home-style canteen
bucketlist.detail: The earthy north-Bengal greens-and-kalai-flour curry — slow-simmered, traditional and almost impossible to find south of Rangpur division.

bucketlist.title: Eat kolai ruti with sidol bhorta
bucketlist.detail: Thick gram-flour rotis with pungent fermented-fish sidol bhorta — the breakfast that fuels the upazila bazaars.

bucketlist.title: Buy aakher gur at a winter haat
bucketlist.detail: North Bengal's sugarcane molasses, pressed and boiled at village mills — used in tea and winter pithas.

bucketlist.title: Read about Shishir Bhattacharjee on home ground
bucketlist.detail: The painter and editorial cartoonist behind some of the country's sharpest satirical work was born here in 1960 — Thakurgaon shapes the wit behind his brush.

bucketlist.title: Walk a Suryapuri orchard at flower-time
bucketlist.detail: Before the fruit, the trees fill with creamy panicles in March — the orchards hum with bees and the air carries the early-summer scent.

foods.name: Suryapuri Mango
foods.description: The slim, golden-orange mango of Baliadangi — sweet, fragrant, and the variety the district is famous for.

foods.name: Pelka
foods.description: Earthy regional curry of greens cooked with small kalai-flour balls — a north-Bengal home-cooking staple.

foods.name: Kolai Ruti
foods.description: Thick gram-flour rotis served hot with sidol bhorta or pickle — the farmer's breakfast across Rangpur division.

foods.name: Sidol Bhorta
foods.description: Pungent fermented-fish mash, pounded with red chili, onion and mustard oil — the partner to kolai ruti.

foods.name: Aakher Gur
foods.description: Sugarcane molasses pressed and boiled at village mills — used in winter pithas and to sweeten tea.

foods.name: Aakher Gur Pitha
foods.description: Winter rice pithas — chitoi and bhapa — drizzled with fresh sugarcane molasses.

foods.name: Tangon River Fish
foods.description: Fresh catch from the Tangon and the smaller northern rivers — small carp and catfish in light mustard curries.

famousPeople.name: Shishir Bhattacharjee
famousPeople.knownFor: Painter, editorial cartoonist and academic — one of Bangladesh's leading satirical artists. Born in Thakurgaon in 1960, trained at Dhaka University and Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda; long-time professor at the Faculty of Fine Art, Dhaka University.

didYouKnow: Thakurgaon became a district on 1 February 1984, carved out of greater Dinajpur — its name is traced to the local Thakur (Brahmin) families who ruled the area before 1879.
The Suryapuri mango tree at Mandumala in Baliadangi — about 200 years old, 80–90 feet tall and spreading over roughly an acre — is claimed as the largest mango tree in Asia.
The Suryapuri mango itself is a Thakurgaon signature: most of the country's Suryapuri orchards sit in Baliadangi upazila.
Jamalpur Zamindar Bari Jame Mosque was built in 1867 with three domes and 28 minarets — its construction was begun before the zamindar's own house was finished.
Painter Shishir Bhattacharjee, one of Bangladesh's most distinctive satirical artists, was born here in 1960.
